```
import java.text.SimpleDateFormat;
import java.util.*;

public class Solution {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Scanner scanner = new Scanner(System.in);
        int n = scanner.nextInt();
        int m = scanner.nextInt();

        String lastStart = null;
        int nextWindowCount = 0;

        while (scanner.hasNextLine()) {
            String[] line = scanner.nextLine().split(":");
            String time = line[1] + " " + line[2] + " " + line[3];

            long currentTime = parseTime(time);
            long timeLimit = parseTime(lastStart) + n * 1000;

            if (currentTime >= timeLimit) {
                nextWindowCount++;
            } else {
                if (lastStart == null || parseTime(lastStart) + n * 1000 > currentTime) {
                    nextWindowCount++;
                }
            }

            if (currentTime >= currentTime - n * 1000) {
                lastStart = time;
                if (nextWindowCount >= m) {
                    break;
                }
            }
        }

        if (nextWindowCount >= m) {
            System.out.println("2012-" + lastStart.split("-")[1] + "-" + lastStart.split("-")[2] + " " + lastStart.split(":")[2].split(" ")[0]);
        } else {
            System.out.println("-1");
        }
    }

    private static long parseTime(String time) {
        SimpleDateFormat sdf = new SimpleDateFormat("yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss");
        Date date = null;
        try {
            date = sdf.parse(time);
        } catch (Exception e) {
            e.printStackTrace();
        }
        return date.getTime();
    }
}
```

```
def get_time(data, seconds):
    # Parse data, convert timestamps to datetime objects
    logs = sorted(data, key=lambda x: datetime.strptime(x, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'))

    cache = {logs[-1]: 1}

    # Compute the running count of warnings in the last 'seconds' seconds
    result = -1

        if i > 0:

        count = cache.get(logs[i], 0) + 1
```
